item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J02045","case1_error":"Reports total beverage volume, 72 ounces, instead of applying the ratio to find 9 ounces of tea.","case2_error":"Omits the 250 papers delivered daily, calculating recycling revenue for only one paper per day.","reason":"The first answers the wrong quantity; the second omits a multiplicity factor while calculating the requested revenue.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02046","case1_error":"Gives unsupported final value 6186 after correct formulas that yield 859 balloons per school.","case2_error":"Gives unsupported final value 60 after correct formulas that yield 110 missed balls.","reason":"Both provide correct setups followed by incorrect final numbers without showing the calculations producing them.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J02047","case1_error":"Treats 70% cheaper as costing 70% of the original price instead of 30%.","case2_error":"After correctly finding 200 days, adds the initial dollar investment to that duration.","reason":"The first misinterprets a percentage discount; the second introduces an invalid addition of money to time.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02048","case1_error":"Divides by four siblings, excluding Jose from the five people sharing the land.","case2_error":"Equates future age to the five-year interval, then unjustifiably identifies the century's length as Gideon's current age.","reason":"The first miscounts recipients; the second confuses an age with a time interval and subsequently with a marble count.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02049","case1_error":"Assumes selling price equals construction cost and subtracts the extra $100,000 twice when calculating additional profit.","case2_error":"Incorrectly evaluates adding $11.53 change to $68.47 as $130.72; the sum is $80.","reason":"The first uses unjustified cost relations and double-counts an expense; the second numerically miscalculates a correctly specified addition.","judgment":"different"}]}
